mode.title: How do you want to install?
mode.blurb: Every answer can be changed later by running `thulu init` again.

identity.title: How do people log in?
identity.blurb: Thulu stores no passwords: people sign in with their company account (SSO) or with GitHub. Without a login, the dashboard only opens from this machine.

database.title: Postgres
database.blurb: Where Thulu keeps everything. The stack ships one ready to use; pick another only if you already run a managed Postgres.
database.blurb_kubernetes: Where Thulu keeps everything. The chart ships none: it needs a Postgres the cluster can reach.

network.title: Public address
network.blurb: The address people open Thulu at in their browser. Sign-in returns to that address, so it has to be exact.

cluster.title: Cluster and isolation
cluster.blurb: Which namespace the chart lands in, and what sandbox agents get. Kata gives every agent its own kernel; gVisor is lighter and shares one.

mcp.title: MCP servers for agents
mcp.blurb: The tools agents call during a run. Each checked server is installed next to the daemon; rerun `thulu init` to change the set.

license.title: Enterprise license (optional)
license.blurb: Unlocks several SSO providers, custom roles, several workspaces and audit log export. Without one, the install runs the community edition.

workspace.title: First workspace
workspace.blurb: Projects, boards and agents live inside a workspace. The setup creates the first one and a key for the CLI and the API.

post_boot.title: GitHub
post_boot.blurb: Without a token, agents read public repos but cannot create branches or open PRs. It can be added later from the dashboard.

engines.title: Engines
engines.blurb: The CLI each agent runs. Each engine has its own agent image, and Claude Code installs itself on the first run: you pick the ones you will use and give each its credential. Each agent picks its engine in Agents.

runner.title: Runner on this machine (optional)
runner.blurb: Whether agents may also run here, outside the containers.

prompts.reverse_proxies: IP or range of the proxy in front of it, so Thulu sees each visitor's real IP (Enter = no proxy)

mode_docker.label: Custom Docker
mode_docker.detail: You choose how it is published (on a domain with HTTPS, or on this machine only), how people sign in (SSO or GitHub), the database and the MCP servers. Agents run in containers next to Thulu.

mode_kubernetes.label: Kubernetes / k3s
mode_kubernetes.detail: For several nodes or a SaaS: writes values for the Helm chart. Agents run as pods isolated in microVMs (Kata by default); runners are off there.

stack_standalone.label: Only on this machine, or behind your own proxy
stack_standalone.detail: The published image with nothing in front, on port 8585. It listens on 127.0.0.1 unless you give another address; HTTPS is up to your proxy. ({file})

identity_oidc.label: OIDC provider (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Keycloak, Google, …)
identity_oidc.detail: Before going on, the setup contacts the provider and checks the URL, so a typo shows up here.

identity_github.label: GitHub OAuth app
identity_github.detail: People sign in with their GitHub account. The token agents push with is asked for later.

identity_none.label: No login (local only)
identity_none.detail: Whoever opens the dashboard is its owner, so it is published on 127.0.0.1 only.

isolation_kata.label: kata-clh: a microVM per agent
isolation_kata.detail: Own kernel per agent. The recommended default for code the operator did not write.

isolation_gvisor.label: gvisor: userspace kernel
isolation_gvisor.detail: Lighter and faster to start; a shared host kernel behind a syscall filter.

isolation_default.label: cluster default, no RuntimeClass
isolation_default.detail: Agents are ordinary containers. Only sensible when the whole cluster is already single-tenant.

stack_caddy.label: Server with a domain and HTTPS
stack_caddy.detail: The published image with Caddy in front, which gets a certificate for your domain on its own. Ports 80 and 443 have to reach this machine. ({file})

mode_quick.label: Quick, on this machine
mode_quick.detail: Docker with the published image, no login, reachable only at 127.0.0.1:8585. It asks for the engines, the runner and GitHub; everything else takes its default and shows up in the summary.

runner_no.label: No, agents run in containers
runner_no.detail: The usual setup. You can add the runner later by running `thulu init` again.

runner_yes.label: Yes, install the runner here
runner_yes.detail: Registers this machine with the workspace, gives it the folders you choose and keeps it running.

review_go.label: Install
review_go.detail: Writes deploy/.env, pulls the images and starts the stack.
review_go.dry_run: Dry run: shows the end without writing or running anything.

review_details.label: Show the deploy/.env changes and the command
review_details.detail: Prints the file's diff and what will run, then asks again.

stack_keep.label: Keep the current one: {file}
stack_keep.detail: The stack an earlier run set up, which compiles Thulu from this checkout. To work on Thulu itself, `make dev` runs the development stack.

mcp.octopus_api: the board for agents: read and update tasks, comments, attachments; acts with the run's own key
mcp.thulu_github: GitHub: pull requests, commits, branches, Actions runs
mcp.thulu_browser: headless Chromium (Playwright): navigate, click, screenshots attached to the task
mcp.thulu_cloud: read-only cloud metrics and logs (GCP, AWS); needs a cloud credential per environment
mcp.thulu_figma: read-only Figma files, frames, renders and comments; needs a Figma token on /credentials

runner.box_body:
The runner is this same program running on your machine and taking agent runs from this Thulu.

• Agents work here, with your git, your tools, your local MCP servers and your `claude` login.
• The code of the runner's projects is not copied to the server: the daemon gets what the agent reports (comments, the files it publishes, the run's log).
• It fits when a repo cannot leave this machine, or when the agent needs something only here: a local database, a simulator, a VPN.
• For now it runs Claude Code only. This setup registers it with the Thulu it installs; against a remote one, use `thulu runner register`.

Without it, agents run in Docker containers, which is the usual setup.
